gaps.gap: No model for items loaded at a station other than the departure station: PEN/LGK return legs and KUL-sourced items on LHR/HKG departures had prep deadlines after the catering had already left KUL.

The inbound-loading cap left no loading window, so F07 MH0003 LHR-KUL's KUL-loaded pajamas, slippers and signature drinks were due after they had left KUL. The PEN/LGK rotation was also hard-wired (now an editable Flight ID).
P-sheets unusable on paper: ~5pt text, 10-20 mm answer boxes, fixed row heights clip real entries, page 1 a third empty, sign-off split under wrong header.
No input for the actual carrying flight of KUL-sourced items on outstation departures, so capped dues ran 2.5-5 h late and the KUL loading itself was never checked.
PEN/LGK return-leg link accepted only agenda flights, so F21 defaulted to an overnight-carried load with dues 26 h early, and clearing it dropped the KUL loading check.
Still ~6.7pt effective print (header wider than table), signature rows < 5 mm, attachment boxes too small to hold an A4 GLD.
Paths to READY without valid evidence: prep checks completed after departure counted, PIC not required, whitespace evidence passed, and N/A could waive physical uplift of meals.
Per-flight Readiness column clipped 'NOT READY – DOCUMENTS OUTSTANDING' on every flight in print.
Round-trip on-board uplift could be confirmed before the carrying flight left KUL; CA status 'Open ' or 'Pending' counted as closed.
P11 cover banner gave a prep deadline (05:45) that contradicted the binding row due (03:50).
Preparation checks were bounded by STD, not the loading point: a batch sensory done after the food had flown out on the KUL carrier still counted.
Placeholder text ('TBC', '-', 'pending') in the Documents sheet counted as the GLD/menu checklist being ON FILE, unlocking READY without a real document.
Evidence like 'photo to follow', 'TBC – will upload' or 'Done' still counted, because placeholders were matched only as whole words.

Text rules matched fragments with spaces removed: 'No defects found' and 'Sensory report BC-017' were rejected, while 'Awaiting…' still passed in N/A justification, batch, result and document attachment.
Negation counted anywhere in the text: '0 discrepancies' and 'fail-safe' were rejected while 'missing, no spares' passed; 'Visually checked' and verifier 'Self' were accepted.
The problem-word rule rejected about a third of natural 'all good' phrasings ('No visible defects', 'No quantity discrepancy') yet passed tallies like 'Missing: 0, Dirty: 2'.
Pending detection still blocked READY without negation ('no CA pending' rejected) and missed future forms ('Photos will be uploaded' accepted as evidence).
Evidence with a reference number plus unlisted not-yet wording ('SF-2210 awaited', 'will be forwarded', 'outstanding') still counted; prep-stage results like 'awaiting loading' were rejected.
'Contains a digit' stood in for 'traceable': 'Checked 14:00' and phone calls passed, while referenced records saying 'expected 24 / actual 24' or 'will not be carried' were blocked.
Any letter-then-digit counted as a reference, so flight numbers, galley codes and dates passed ('Checked onboard MH0727'), while real IDs with a space ('DN 88213', 'seal no 88213') failed.

Documents helper formulas nested ~80 levels (over Excel's 64, which would trigger a repair and strip them); 'Checked 1400 hrs' and 'MH 0727' still counted as references; 'Not yet loaded' passed on on-board rows.
'Chkd 1400 hrs', 'Qty 180' and 'on call 1400' still counted as references; 'to be loaded' passed on on-board rows; 'seal numbers 88213-88220' and 'QA form F-2210' were rejected.
Word-list fixes kept missing variants ('Verified by CSM 1400' accepted, 'GLD-MH0727-A' rejected). User decision: replace free-text evidence with a structured type + ID.
Evidence ID shape check too loose: any '/' counted as a link, and flight numbers, dates, revisions and times passed as IDs; role-only verifiers (QA, CSM) accepted.
The mandatory Evidence type had no place on paper and printed run together with the ID, so a hand-filled pack could not be transcribed reliably.
On the six KUL-sourced / round-trip packs the cover overflowed page 1, splitting signatures from names and pushing the checklist to page 3.
A plain Pass whose own result said 'menu cards not delivered' counted as complete and the flight went READY; the evidence-ID check was also easy to fool and rejected genuine IDs.
Whether a clarification or N/A line counted was decided by keyword lists on free text, so 'query raised' or 'N/A – unknown at this time' could make a flight READY.
A preparation line confirmed 'carried' while its on-board line was N/A 'not carried', so a flight went READY without the item ever being checked on board.
KUL-sourced packs gave the PIC nowhere to write the carrying flight and its KUL departure, which the workbook needs before those lines can pass.
An N/A counted whatever its time – even recorded after departure or with no time at all.
The loading time that caps preparation lines was taken from any on-board row, so a correctly confirmed 'not carried' clarification made the whole flight's preparation invalid.

An answer that moves an item's uplift station (e.g. toiletry kits loaded at LHR, sales cart at KUL) could not be recorded, so the check station, due time and loading cap could not follow it – solved with the Settings station-confirmation table (user's choice).
